question: What do yogins recognize in the cessation of agitation?
premises: Yogins call that state the immortal supreme abode.
It is found in the cessations of the beginning and end of agitation.
That same state is also called the supreme nectar.
inference: Therefore the still point beyond agitation is identified as both supreme abode and supreme nectar.
uncertainties: The plural locative virāmeṣu may indicate repeated moments of cessation rather than distinct places.
plain_english: Yogins declare that this is the immortal, supreme abode. In the cessations at the beginning and end of agitation, that very state is known as the supreme nectar.
